## Overview
### Introduction to Google: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview
The Google: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview is a standard-tier model released by Google on 2024-01-01. This model is not open source, providing developers with a robust tool for various natural language processing tasks. The architecture of Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview is designed to handle large context windows of up to 1,048,576 tokens and generate outputs of up to 65,536 tokens. With a knowledge cutoff of 2023-12, this model is well-equipped to handle a wide range of applications, including chat, text generation, coding, analysis, and summarization.

### Strengths and Use Cases
The main strengths of the Google: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview lie in its capabilities, which include text, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs. These capabilities make it an ideal choice for tasks such as chat, text generation, coding, analysis, RAG pipelines, and summarization. The model's performance is backed by its benchmarks, including an MMLU score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO score of 1200. With its pricing structure, developers can expect to pay $0.25 per 1M tokens for input and $1.5 per 1M tokens for output. For example, 1,000 calls with an average of 500 tokens would cost approximately $0.0009.

### Pricing and Cost Considerations
The pricing model for the Google: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview is straightforward, with costs associated with input and output tokens. There are no costs for cached input or batch input. The cost examples provided indicate that the model can be used at a relatively low cost, with 10,000 calls costing $0.009 and 100,000 calls costing $0.09.
